content: Ofloxacin is an antibiotic prescribed to treat specific bacterial infections, including pneumonia, bronchitis, venereal diseases (VD), and infections of the prostate, skin, and urinary tract. It is not effective against colds, flu, or other viral infections. Ofloxacin is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken every 12 hours (twice daily) with or without food for a duration of 3 to 10 days, depending on the infection. Some infections may require treatment for up to 6 weeks or longer. For venereal diseases, a single dose is usually prescribed. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take ofloxacin exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Swallow the tablets with a full glass of water. Continue taking the medication even if you feel better, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking ofloxacin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ofloxacin or other related antibiotics such as ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, or nalidixic acid, among others. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. Mention specific medications such as other antibiotics, blood thinners like warfarin, cancer chemotherapy agents, cimetidine, cyclosporine, diabetes medications, probenecid, sucralfate, or theophylline. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. If you are taking mineral supplements, antacids containing aluminum, calcium, or magnesium, didanosine chewable/buffered tablets or oral solution, sucralfate, or vitamins containing iron or zinc, take ofloxacin at least two hours before or two hours after these medications. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease, diabetes, epilepsy, colitis, stomach problems, vision issues, heart disease, or a history of stroke. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking ofloxacin, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking ofloxacin. Be aware that ofloxacin may cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or fatigue. Avoid driving or operating dangerous machinery until you know how the medication affects you. Minimize unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and wear protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as ofloxacin may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. Drink at least eight full glasses of water or other fluids daily while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Ofloxacin may cause side effects. Mild side effects include upset stomach, diarrhea, vomiting, stomach pain, headache, restlessness, and difficulty sleeping. Contact your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. These include skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face or throat, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, pale or dark stools, blood in the urine, unusual tiredness, sunburn, seizures, vaginal infections, vision changes, or pain, inflammation, or rupture of a tendon. Report any unusual problems to your doctor while taking this medication. Store ofloxacin in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat, moisture, and light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests may be required to monitor your response to ofloxacin. Inform your doctor and laboratory personnel that you are taking this medication before undergoing any tests. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of ofloxacin, contact your doctor.
